parts:
Hi,

I am about to embark on installing r, shiny and rstudio in AWS using centos (my employer has a thing about using Ubuntu so have to switch it all to centos)

Or is there an updated version of this?

CentOS step by step Installation Instructions

the current install page refers to installing epel, then a few simple commands - Is this all thats really needed to get shiny up and running?
http://www.rstudio.com/shiny/server/install-opensource

there was quite a few steps with Ubuntu server (as well as the wiki doc shows quite a few more steps) 
this makes me think I am going to delete and rebuild a few times so hoping there is some advice here so i don't have to go through this process :)

lastly, is there an AMI that we can use to just install it all? that would be useful.

cheers

messages.author: bbc57ffa8a14ad13
messages.subject: Re: centos AWS shiny and rstudio install instructions
parts:
Hi Narbeh,

Yup, it should be that simple. It sounds like you installed previously before we provided installers; there were a few dozen steps to setup back then. Now that we have installers it should be as simple as installing R then running a couple of extra commands. The installer will do the rest.

Let us know if you have any trouble! I don't know of an AMI that's updated and available, and we don't have anything official at the moment.

Jeff

messages.author: bbc57ffa8a14ad13
messages.subject: Re: centos AWS shiny and rstudio install instructions
parts:
You'll want to check a few things if you can't get in to the server.

  1. The Shiny Server log at /var/log/shiny-server.log If Shiny Server is having problems, they'll be listed here. If everything looks ok here, then it's most likely not a Shiny Server issue.
  2. For Amazon AWS, you'll want to check the security group your instance is running in to make sure that port 3838 is open and available.
  3. Some distributions ship with a firewall like iptables enabled by default. You'll need to be sure that port 3838 isn't being blocked by your machine.

If none of those work, is SELinux enabled on your machine?

Jeff
